# Error and warning codes

<!-- Generated by @internal/docs (target: errors). Run `yarn fix` to update. -->

Errors print as `error[E_CODE]: message` on stderr and make the command exit non-zero. Warnings print as `warning[W_CODE]: message` (prefixed with the plugin name when a plugin raised it) and do not stop the command. Pass `--verbose` to print debug output and, for unexpected errors, the stack and cause.

Codes are only added, never removed or renamed. Plugins that define their own codes document them separately.

## Errors

### E_BASE_REQUIRED

Cause: `tallyrelease run` could not determine the build base because the request for the last successful run failed (`W_FORGE_ERROR`). Planning without a base would use the wrong range, so `run` stops before tagging or pushing anything.

Fix: Re-run once the forge is reachable, or pass `--base <ref>` explicitly. Check that the token (`--token` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`) is valid.

### E_BASE_UNRESOLVED

Cause: A base ref does not resolve to a commit, or the `pull_request` event has no merge base with HEAD. The ref comes from `--base`, `pull_request.base.sha` or `merge_group.base_sha` of the event payload.

Fix: Check the ref passed to `--base` and make sure it exists locally (`git fetch origin <ref>`). In CI, check out the full history with `fetch-depth: 0`.

### E_BRANCH_RULE

Cause: An entry of `branches` is invalid. The `name` is empty, uses a token other than `{major}` or `{minor}`, repeats a token, uses `{minor}` without `{major}` or has an unbalanced brace. Or `unit` and `group` are both set, `unit` or `group` is set on a rule that is not a `maintenance` rule with `{major}`, or `unit` names a unit that is not released, is in a group or does not exist, or `group` names an unknown group.

Fix: Correct the rule named in the message. Use either `unit` (ungrouped released unit) or `group`, only on `line: maintenance` rules whose `name` contains `{major}`, and name a unit or group that exists in the config.

### E_CAP

Cause: On a maintenance branch, a release item would leave the line of its current version, for example a breaking change or `Release-As` on a `release/1.x` branch. The message lists the offending commits.

Fix: Remove or reword the commits that exceed the limit, for example by moving them to the default branch, or use a `Release-As` value inside the line. If the branch should release a new major, use a `default` line rule with a `channel` instead of a `maintenance` rule.

### E_CAP_BASE

Cause: On a maintenance branch, the unit or group named by the rule (or the only release item) is at a version outside the line captured by the branch name. Typically the branch was cut from or merged with a commit that carries a newer tag.

Fix: Cut the branch from the last release of that line, or remove the newer commits from it. Set `unit` or `group` on the rule to name the item the line applies to.

### E_CHANNEL_DUPLICATE

Cause: Two `branches` rules set the same `channel`.

Fix: Give each rule a distinct `channel`, or remove the `channel` from one of them.

### E_CHANNEL_INVALID

Cause: A rule's `channel` is not a valid prerelease identifier: it must match `[0-9A-Za-z-]+`, contain a letter or dash, and use only `{major}` and `{minor}` tokens that the rule's `name` captures. The same code is raised when the channel does not form a valid prerelease for a version.

Fix: Use letters, digits and dashes only (for example `beta` or `rc-{major}`) and capture any token you use in the rule `name`.

### E_CHANNEL_WILDCARD

Cause: A `branches` rule sets a `channel` while its `name` contains `*`, so the channel would be ambiguous.

Fix: Remove the `*` from the rule `name`, or remove the `channel` from that rule.

### E_CONFIG

Cause: The config file is not valid YAML, does not match the schema (unknown key, wrong type), or fails a semantic check: a unit sets `releasePr` while being in a group, a `tags.floating` format uses a token other than `{id}`, `{major}` or `{minor}`, or a `versionFiles` entry has a bad `file` or `pattern`.

Fix: Fix the key named in the message. A `versionFiles` `pattern` needs literal text and either `{version}` or the `{major}`, `{minor}`, `{patch}` tokens (not mixed), and `file` must be a repo-relative path without `..`. Set `releasePr` on the group instead of on its members.

### E_CONFIG_MISSING

Cause: The config file does not exist at the path given by `--config` (default `tallyrelease.yaml`) in the repository root.

Fix: Create `tallyrelease.yaml`, for example with `plugins: { node: {} }`, or pass the right path with `--config`.

### E_CWD_MISSING

Cause: The directory given by `--cwd` (or the current directory) does not exist.

Fix: Pass an existing repository root with `--cwd`, or run the command from it.

### E_DUPLICATE_ROOT

Cause: Two plugins discover a unit at the same root.

Fix: Disable one of the plugins under `plugins`, or move one of the packages so each root is discovered once.

### E_DUPLICATE_UNIT

Cause: Two units resolve to the same id.

Fix: Give one of them a distinct `id` in `units.<root>`.

### E_EDGE_SELF

Cause: A dependency edge points from a unit to itself. The message names the source, either a plugin or `config` (a `deps` entry).

Fix: Remove the edge, or correct `from` or `to` in the `deps` entry.

### E_EDGE_UNKNOWN_UNIT

Cause: A dependency edge names a unit id that does not exist. The message names the source, either a plugin or `config` (a `deps` entry).

Fix: Correct `from` or `to` in the `deps` entry so both are existing unit ids.

### E_GITHUB_EVENT

Cause: `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` is set but the file cannot be read or parsed as JSON.

Fix: Check that `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` points to the event payload file of the GitHub Actions run, or unset it when running locally.

### E_GITHUB_OUTPUT

Cause: `--github-output` was passed but `GITHUB_OUTPUT` is not set. For `plan` and `run`, it is also raised when neither `--out` nor `RUNNER_TEMP` is available.

Fix: Run inside GitHub Actions, or set `GITHUB_OUTPUT` to a writable file. For `plan` and `run`, also pass `--out <file>`.

### E_GIT_DATE

Cause: A commit has a committer date that cannot be parsed.

Fix: Check the commit named in the message with `git log --format=%cI <sha>`. Rewrite the history if the date is corrupt, or plan with a `--base` after that commit.

### E_GIT_READ

Cause: A git read of a file at a ref failed, for example when `git cat-file` cannot find the blob or the ref. The message includes git's reason.

Fix: Check that the ref and path exist (`git cat-file -e <ref>:<path>`). In CI, fetch enough history with `fetch-depth: 0`.

### E_GROUP_NOT_RELEASED

Cause: A group member is a unit that is not released.

Fix: Set `release: true` on the unit (or `defaults.release: true`), or remove it from the group's `units` or `tags` selection.

### E_GROUP_OVERLAP

Cause: A unit is a member of two groups.

Fix: Adjust `groups.<name>.units` and `groups.<name>.tags` so every unit belongs to at most one group.

### E_GROUP_SCHEME

Cause: Members of a group use different version schemes.

Fix: Set the same `scheme` on all members of the group, or split the group.

### E_GROUP_UNKNOWN_UNIT

Cause: A group's `units` list names a unit id that does not exist.

Fix: Correct the id in `groups.<name>.units`.

### E_HEAD_UNRESOLVED

Cause: The ref given by `--head` (or `HEAD` for `shadow`) does not resolve to a commit.

Fix: Pass an existing commit to `--head`, and fetch it first if it is not available locally.

### E_INITIAL_VERSION

Cause: A unit's `initialVersion` is not a valid version for its scheme.

Fix: Set `initialVersion` (on the unit or in `defaults`) to a version its scheme accepts, for example `1.0.0` for `semver`.

### E_INTERNAL

Cause: An unexpected error that tallyrelease did not classify, such as a failed git push, a filesystem error or a bug.

Fix: Re-run with `--verbose` to see the stack and cause. If it is not a local problem, report it with that output.

### E_NOT_A_REPO

Cause: The working directory is not inside a git repository.

Fix: Run the command from a git checkout, or pass the repository root with `--cwd`.

### E_NOT_REPO_ROOT

Cause: The working directory is below the repository root.

Fix: Run the command from the repository root, or pass it with `--cwd`.

### E_NO_FORGE

Cause: `pr` or `release` has no forge token, or the forge repository cannot be determined from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` or the `origin` remote.

Fix: Pass `--token` or set `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and set `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` (`owner/repo`) or add an `origin` remote with a GitHub URL.

### E_NO_HEAD

Cause: `HEAD` does not resolve to a commit because the repository has no commits.

Fix: Create an initial commit before running the command.

### E_PATH_OUTSIDE_ROOT

Cause: A file to write, such as a version file, is the repository root itself or resolves outside it.

Fix: Use repo-relative paths without `..` for version files, in the config and in plugin options.

### E_PENDING_RECONCILE

Cause: `pr` found merged release PRs that have not been tagged yet, so opening a new release PR would use stale state.

Fix: Run `tallyrelease release` first to tag and publish the merged release PRs, then run `pr` again.

### E_PLUGIN_API

Cause: A plugin uses an API version that this tallyrelease does not support.

Fix: Use a plugin built for this version of tallyrelease, or upgrade or downgrade the CLI to match the plugin.

### E_PLUGIN_HOOK

Cause: A plugin hook (such as `discover`, `edges`, `intent` or `write`) threw an error. The message names the plugin, the hook and the reason.

Fix: Fix the cause given in the message, usually a malformed manifest or version file in the repository, or the plugin options in `plugins.<name>`.

### E_PLUGIN_LOAD

Cause: A plugin set with `plugins.<name>.path` could not be loaded: the file is missing, outside the repository, fails to import, does not export a plugin, or exports a plugin with another name. A built-in plugin (`node`, `php`, `kustomize`) that sets `path` is also rejected, since built-ins cannot be replaced.

Fix: Check the path (relative to the repository root) and that the file's default export is a plugin whose `name` is the config key. Remove `path` from built-in plugins, or use another name.

### E_PLUGIN_NAME

Cause: A plugin name does not match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`, or uses the name `core`, which is reserved.

Fix: Rename the plugin to lowercase letters, digits and dashes starting with a letter, and not `core`.

### E_PLUGIN_OPTIONS

Cause: The options under `plugins.<name>` fail the plugin's option validation.

Fix: Fix the options named in the message, or remove them.

### E_PLUGIN_UNKNOWN

Cause: `plugins` lists a name that matches no built-in plugin (`node`, `php`, `kustomize`).

Fix: Correct the plugin name in `plugins`, or remove the entry.

### E_PUSH_LEASE

Cause: A push was rejected because a remote ref moved since tallyrelease read it, usually a concurrent run or a commit pushed to the release branch.

Fix: Re-run the command so it reads the current remote state. Avoid running concurrent jobs for the same branch.

### E_RELEASE_ITEM_NAME

Cause: A release item (a group or an ungrouped released unit) has a name that cannot be used in a release PR branch: it is `shared`, starts or ends with `.`, ends with `.lock`, contains `..`, or a unit id equals a group name.

Fix: Rename the unit (`units.<root>.id`) or the group so the name is valid and unique.

### E_RELEASE_PR_SPLIT_EDGE

Cause: A dependency edge that propagates a patch release connects two release items that are in different release PRs.

Fix: Put both items in the same release PR with `releasePr` (or `defaults.releasePr`), group them under `groups`, or set `propagate: rebuild` on the dependent unit.

### E_ROOT_INVALID

Cause: A unit root, such as a key under `units` or a root discovered by a plugin, is absolute or contains `..` segments.

Fix: Use repo-relative paths without `..`.

### E_ROOT_MISSING

Cause: The root of a unit does not exist in the working tree, for example a key under `units` that points to a missing directory.

Fix: Create the directory, or correct or remove the `units` key.

### E_SCHEME_CLASH

Cause: Two plugins register a version scheme under the same name.

Fix: Disable one of the plugins under `plugins`.

### E_SCHEME_UNKNOWN

Cause: A released unit's `scheme` is not registered by any enabled plugin.

Fix: Correct `scheme` on the unit, or enable the plugin that provides it under `plugins`. The default scheme is `semver`.

### E_SHADOW_INPUT

Cause: The release-please manifest (`--manifest`) or config (`--rp-config`) read by `shadow` is not valid JSON, or is not an object (of version strings for the manifest).

Fix: Fix the JSON in the file named in the message.

### E_SHADOW_MISMATCH

Cause: `shadow --strict` found rows of the comparison between the plan and the release-please manifest change that are not labelled as expected differences.

Fix: Inspect the report (`--out` or `--summary`) and resolve or label the differing rows, or run without `--strict`.

### E_SHALLOW_BASE

Cause: A base commit is missing from a shallow clone, or has no common history with HEAD in it.

Fix: Fetch the full history, for example `fetch-depth: 0` in `actions/checkout` or `git fetch --unshallow`.

### E_TAG_EXISTS

Cause: A release tag already exists at a different commit, locally or on the remote. With `--dry-run` this is detected without writing.

Fix: Check whether the release was already tagged by another commit. Delete or move the stale tag only if it is wrong (`git tag -d <tag>` and `git push origin :refs/tags/<tag>`), then re-run.

### E_TAG_FORMAT

Cause: A unit's `tagFormat` does not contain `{version}` exactly once.

Fix: Set `tagFormat` (on the unit or in `defaults`) to a template with a single `{version}`, for example `{id}-v{version}`.

### E_TAG_FORMAT_OVERLAP

Cause: Two released units render the same tag format, or one existing tag matches the format of more than one released unit.

Fix: Give the units distinct `tagFormat` values, usually by including `{id}`.

### E_UNIT_GLOB

Cause: A glob key under `units` uses `*` inside a path segment instead of as a whole segment, or sets `id`, `include`, `exclude` or `versionFiles`, which globs cannot set.

Fix: Use `*` only as a whole path segment (`packages/*`), and move those fields to an exact key.

### E_UNIT_ID

Cause: A unit id contains characters other than letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, or is `.` or `..`.

Fix: Set a valid `id` in `units.<root>`.

### E_UNIT_TAG

Cause: An entry in a unit's `tags` contains characters other than letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

Fix: Rename the label in `units.<root>.tags`.

### E_UNIT_UNKNOWN

Cause: `explain` was given a unit id that does not exist.

Fix: Pass an existing unit id. List ids with `tallyrelease graph`.

### E_VERSION_FILE_CLAIM

Cause: A file is the version file of two units, or is both a plugin version file and a `versionFiles` template target.

Fix: Remove the duplicate `versionFiles` entry, or set one file per unit.

### E_VERSION_FILE_MISSING

Cause: A version file of a unit (from a plugin or a `versionFiles` entry) does not exist in the commit the release is based on.

Fix: Create the file, or correct or remove the `versionFiles` entry.

### E_VERSION_INVALID

Cause: Bumping a version produced a string that is not a valid version. This does not happen for a valid current version.

Fix: Report it as a bug with the version named in the message and the `--verbose` output.

## Warnings

### W_CYCLE

Cause: The dependency graph has a cycle. The message shows the path.

Fix: Remove one of the edges, for example a `deps` entry. The plan still runs, but the order of units in a cycle is not meaningful.

### W_EFFECT_SKIPPED

Cause: An effect command (`version`, `pr` or `release`) did nothing because it ran on a `pull_request` or `merge_group` event, or on a branch with no matching `branches` rule.

Fix: Run the command on a push to a branch matched by a `branches` rule, or add a rule for the branch.

### W_FORGE_ERROR

Cause: A forge request failed. Either the last successful workflow run could not be read (the build base is unknown), or the PRs and releases of released commits could not be read for `plan`.

Fix: Check the token (`--token` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`), its permissions and the forge status, or pass `--base <ref>`.

### W_GROUP_EMPTY

Cause: A group in `groups` selects no released unit through `units` or `tags`, so it is dropped.

Fix: Add member ids to `groups.<name>.units`, tag units with a label listed in `groups.<name>.tags`, or remove the group.

### W_HEAD_BRANCH

Cause: `--head` was used without `--branch`, so the plan uses the branch rule for the current branch instead of the branch the commit belonged to.

Fix: Pass `--branch <name>` to choose the branch rule.

### W_INITIAL_BELOW_PRERELEASE

Cause: A unit's initial version does not exceed an existing prerelease tag of that unit.

Fix: Raise `initialVersion` above the prerelease tag named in the message, or remove the stale tag.

### W_NO_BRANCH_RULE

Cause: No `branches` rule matches the branch, so versions in the plan are null.

Fix: Add a rule for the branch under `branches`, for example `{ name: main, line: default }`, or pass `--branch`.

### W_NO_FORGE

Cause: There is no forge token, so the last successful run cannot be read and the base falls back to what is available locally.

Fix: Pass `--token` or set `GITHUB_TOKEN`, or pass `--base <ref>`.

### W_NO_LAST_SUCCESS

Cause: The forge has no successful push run of this workflow on this branch that is an ancestor of HEAD, so there is no base.

Fix: Expected on the first run. Otherwise, check that the workflow succeeded on this branch before, or pass `--base <ref>`.

### W_NO_MATCHING_TAG

Cause: A released unit has no tag matching its `tagFormat`, but an existing tag contains its id.

Fix: Rename the tag or set `tagFormat` on the unit so it matches existing tags.

### W_NO_RELEASED_UNITS

Cause: A branch rule matches, but no unit is released.

Fix: Set `release: true` on units, or `defaults.release: true`.

### W_NO_WORKFLOW_CONTEXT

Cause: `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF` or `GITHUB_REF_NAME` is missing, so the last successful run cannot be looked up.

Fix: Run inside GitHub Actions, or pass `--base <ref>`.

### W_PLUGIN

Cause: A plugin logged a warning. The text is prefixed with the plugin name.

Fix: Follow the message. It usually points at a manifest or option the plugin could not use.

### W_PR_HEAD_BEHIND

Cause: HEAD is not the tip of the base branch on the forge, so `pr` leaves the release PRs unchanged.

Fix: Run `pr` on the latest commit of the branch, for example in the workflow triggered by the newest push.

### W_RELEASED_NO_BASE

Cause: The build base is unknown, so `released` in the plan only lists releases at HEAD and leaves out earlier releases on the first-parent chain.

Fix: Pass `--base <ref>` or make the base resolvable (see `W_NO_FORGE` and `W_NO_LAST_SUCCESS`).

### W_RELEASE_AS_CONFLICT

Cause: Several different `Release-As` values apply to a unit. The newest valid one wins and the message names it.

Fix: Remove the extra `Release-As` footers if the winner is not the intended one.

### W_RELEASE_AS_IGNORED

Cause: A `Release-As` footer is ignored because its commit is not attributed to a released unit, or it names a unit that is not released.

Fix: Name a released unit (`Release-As: <unit>@<version>`), or remove the footer.

### W_RELEASE_AS_INVALID

Cause: A `Release-As` value is not a version of the unit's scheme, or is a prerelease, or does not exceed the unit's current version. It is ignored.

Fix: Correct the footer value in the commit message, or drop it.

### W_RELEASE_AS_UNKNOWN

Cause: A `Release-As: <unit>@<version>` footer names a unit that does not exist.

Fix: Correct the unit id in the footer.

### W_RELEASE_NOT_BUILT

Cause: A release of a unit is at HEAD, but the unit is not in the build set. It is listed as a catch-up.

Fix: Build and publish the unit for that release, or ignore the warning if it was already built.

### W_SHADOW_INPUT_MISSING

Cause: A file passed to `shadow` with `--manifest` or `--rp-config` does not exist at the compared commit.

Fix: Correct the path, or omit the flag to use the default file name.

### W_SHADOW_SKIPPED

Cause: `shadow` skipped the comparison, either because the manifest did not change in the compared commit or because a maintenance limit (`E_CAP` or `E_CAP_BASE`) applies. The message gives the reason.

Fix: Nothing to do for a commit that did not touch the manifest. For a limit, see `E_CAP` or `E_CAP_BASE`.

### W_TAG_UNKNOWN

Cause: A `--tag` value of `affected` is not a label on any unit.

Fix: Correct the value, or add the label to `units.<root>.tags`.

### W_UNIT_GLOB_UNMATCHED

Cause: A glob key under `units` matches no discovered unit. Globs never create units.

Fix: Correct the glob, or remove it.

### W_UNIT_UNKNOWN

Cause: An intent source of a plugin names a unit id that does not exist.

Fix: Correct the unit id in the intent source, or add the unit to the config.

### W_VERSION_FILE_NO_MATCH

Cause: A `versionFiles` `pattern` of a unit matches nothing in its file, so the file is not updated for the release.

Fix: Make `pattern` match the text that holds the previous version, or remove the entry.
